layers.note: A rosette scattered on rocky slopes among desert shrubs and grassland.

moisture.note: Dry, sandy to gravelly ground on granitic or volcanic soils.

heat_load.note: Any aspect; on the desert edge mostly cooler, higher slopes.

elevation_m.note: 700 to 2,100 m (Flora of North America); 3,000 to 7,000 feet in Arizona (Kearney and Peebles). Most plants grow above the bajada, on the mountain slopes; the bajada is at its lower edge.

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 4 to 12 °C; gone below 1 °C and above 14 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −12 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −17 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 22 to 32 °C; gone below 19 °C, where summers are too short, and above 34 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 4,000 to 7,800 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 3,000.

degree_days_5.note: About 2,400 to 6,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 1,700.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.12 to 0.5, gone by 0.08 and above 0.65.

summer_rain.note: Needs the monsoon's summer rain: from about 0.3 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone below 0.2; up to about 0.65, gone by 0.75.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Golden-flowered agave grows only in central and southern Arizona, in desert scrub, grassland, pinyon-juniper and oak woodland (Flora of North America). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
